rounds.text: S P Apparels Ltd demonstrates superior capital efficiency compared to its peers, with an ROA of 6.1% against a sector benchmark of 3.37% and an ROCE of 12.82% versus 8.39% [E8, E10]. This operational strength is underscored by a robust cash conversion ratio of 2.07x, confirming that reported profits are fully backed by actual cash flow [E34]. The company is actively positioning for future expansion, evidenced by a 50% increase in capital work-in-progress [E40]. Furthermore, the stock exhibits strong technical momentum, trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, while maintaining a high relative-strength rating of 78 [E50, E51]. Conceded: the company faces headwinds with a 1% growth in trailing twelve-month sales and a 3% decline in profit growth over the same period [E17, E21]. Despite these short-term fluctuations, the business benefits from a sector-wide tailwind, and institutional money flow remains positive [E44, E71].

The business is currently showing clear signs of fundamental deceleration, with compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months dropping to a negligible 1% [E17] and compounded profit growth contracting by -3% over the same period [E21]. Furthermore, earnings growth is explicitly flagged as decelerating [E68], operating margins are described as inconsistent over the last two years [E32], and the trailing operating margin has compressed by 1 percentage point compared to three years earlier [E30]. This lack of top-line momentum and earnings contraction coincides with rising financial obligations, as total borrowings have increased to Rs 450 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 419 Cr a year prior [E39]. Valuation multiples also look extended on a relative basis, with the EV/EBITDA trading at 11.43x against a sector benchmark of 9x [E11]. Insider alignment is moving in the wrong direction, evidenced by promoter holding declining to 59.82% in September 2026 from 61.93% in December 2023 [E41], alongside a further drop of 1.99% noted over the last quarter [E60]. Conceded: [E45] and [E46], which point to a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 1750 per share and a significant margin of safety.

While the bear highlights short-term deceleration, it ignores the company's superior efficiency and structural improvements. The contraction in TTM growth [E17, E21] is countered by a robust 5-year compounded sales growth of 19% and profit growth of 18% [E15, E19], proving the business has a proven track record of long-term expansion. Furthermore, the company is significantly more efficient than its peers, boasting an ROA of 6.1% against a sector benchmark of 3.37% [E8] and an ROCE of 12.82% compared to 8.39% [E10]. The concern regarding borrowings [E39] is mitigated by the company's strong cash generation, with operating cash flow of Rs 209 Cr and free cash flow of Rs 103 Cr in Mar 2026 [E35, E36], alongside a massive improvement in working capital efficiency from 42.5 days to 24.2 days [E59]. Conceded: the bear is correct that promoter holding has declined [E41, E60], operating margins are currently inconsistent [E32], and the EV/EBITDA multiple is higher than the sector benchmark [E11]. However, the bear overlooks that institutional money flow is currently positive [E44] and the stock is technically strong, trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E50].

Conceded: the bull correctly highlights the 5-year sales growth of 19% and profit growth of 18% [E15, E19]. However, leaning on these historical figures ignores the sharp deceleration evident in trailing twelve-month compounded sales growth dropping to 1% and profits contracting by -3% [E17, E21], compounded by the screen explicitly flagging that earnings growth is decelerating [E68]. While the bull points to strong cash flow and working capital compression [E35, E36, E59], it glosses over the rising debt burden with borrowings increasing to Rs 450 Cr from Rs 419 Cr a year earlier [E39], alongside a low historical return on equity of 11.4% over the last three years [E61] and a negligible dividend payout of 2.49% of profits [E62]. Furthermore, the bull minimizes structural insider detachment by dismissing the promoter holding reduction from 61.93% down to 59.82% [E41], which is further exacerbated by domestic institutions cutting their stake from 19.08% to 15.84% [E43]. Finally, while the stock trades above its moving averages [E50], this technical strength obscures fundamental headwinds including inconsistent yearly and quarterly operating margins [E32, E33] and a premium EV/EBITDA multiple of 11.43x compared to the sector benchmark of 9x [E11].
